topics.label: Introduction to inflammation initiation and resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how innate immune receptors distinguish signs of infection and damage through the properties and locations of the signals they recognise.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor pathways and inflammatory activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific pattern recognition receptor systems translate microbial or damage signals into inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow how activated sentinel cells generate inflammatory signals that mobilise immune cells to the site of infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how drainage from infected tissues enables dendritic cells to initiate adaptive immune responses in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a life-threatening systemic response.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation subsides through the loss of activating stimuli and the increasing influence of inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine recovery of inflamed tissue and why persistent inflammation can remain when damage or infection cannot be fully eliminated.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next lecture.
